MCD.rationale: MCD presents a high-quality franchise business with elite margins (~90% gross, ~45% operating), solid YoY revenue growth (+9.4%) and EPS growth (+6.9%) in Q1 2026, and strong cash conversion (OCF/NI = 1.22x). The stock has de-rated ~12% over the past quarter to $284.77, sitting in the lower quartile of its 365-day range ($271.85–$341.75), driven by rising rates and macro headwinds rather than fundamental deterioration. The qualitative franchise quality is high — 95% franchised, real-estate-backed, $7.2B FY2025 FCF, 51 consecutive years of dividend growth, and a growing digital loyalty flywheel. However, the case is tempered by: (1) all primary valuation ratios (PE, P/S, EV/EBIT, FCF yield) are non-functional in the supplied data, preventing a rigorous valuation-versus-history assessment — the qual report cites P/E ~23x from external sources but this cannot be verified from the quantitative pack; (2) structural risks including negative equity (-$1.29B), traffic competition from grocery channels, franchisee cost pressures, and the lowest ACSI score among QSR peers; (3) moderate growth trajectory (1-3% comps, unit expansion toward 50K by 2027) rather than acceleration. The Q1 2026 EPS beat ($2.83 vs $2.74 consensus) and institutional buying (Capital World Investors adding shares) provide modest near-term support, but no strong dated catalyst exists for a material re-rating. Net: solid fundamentals and trajectory at a likely reasonable valuation, but the valuation data gap and structural risks cap conviction at mildly positive.
